sections.heading: Business objectives and stakeholders in Introduction to Business
paragraphs: Business objectives and stakeholders is studied here as a specific part of Introduction to Business. Begin by defining the term precisely and identifying the problem it helps explain or solve. Keep the scope narrow: related ideas may interact with it, but they are not interchangeable.

Economics studies choices under scarcity and how incentives shape allocation. Separate a movement along a curve, caused by a change in a variable already on an axis, from a shift of the entire curve caused by another determinant. State whether a claim is positive (testable) or normative (value-based).

For this topic, distinguish the central principle from its assumptions. Ask: what is given, what must be inferred or calculated, what evidence would support the conclusion, and in what circumstances would the conclusion no longer hold? At introductory level, establish accurate definitions first, then explain the relationship between concepts and practise a worked example. Be able to explain the idea in your own words rather than memorising a phrase.

sections.heading: Worked application
paragraphs: If demand rises while supply is unchanged, the demand curve shifts right. At the old price there is excess demand, which creates upward pressure on price. The new equilibrium generally has a higher price and higher quantity, provided the usual upward-sloping supply and downward-sloping demand assumptions hold.
